As a side note, the parent class inheritance was implemented as an instance, which allows for the whole object to be allocated in 1 malloc call (giving one derived class pointer to keep track of), but requires you to manually initialize each inherited data member instead of using the parent class constructor to get a parent class pointer. It's not wrong by any means, it's just a tradeoff you make in keeping an instance instead of a pointer.

This implementation correctly applies struct composition and vtable-based polymorphism to model inheritance in C. The design favors a single allocation, clear memory layout, and explicit control over initialization. While it requires careful manual setup of base fields and the vtable, the approach is well-executed, readable, and appropriate for low-level systems-style object modeling.
